summary: Partial final choice & duplicate tokens observed after CDN idle probe during streaming reconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports SSE streaming sessions that briefly stall during a CDN idle-probe window and then reconnect. After reconnect, the client sees a duplicated short token sequence followed by the final choice missing the last grapheme (cut mid-codepoint).

Impact:
- A subset of streaming responses (approx 3-4% for this customer during peak) show a short duplicate token sequence immediately before the final chunk, and the final output sometimes ends with an incomplete grapheme/byte (rendered as replacement char in some clients).
- Affects user-visible messages in ByteForge's chat integration; user experience degraded. No full crashes but increased support tickets.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east-1) behind CloudFront + internal streaming proxy + nginx h2 edge in customer's infra. Customer on self-serve account using Redwood hosted API.

Observed behavior:
- Client connects via SSE. After ~15-45s of idle, CloudFront issues an idle probe and the connection briefly enters a probe/half-close. The client receives a short duplicate sequence (e.g., "...ing. ing.") then final choice truncated (last Unicode grapheme missing).

Expected behavior:
- Streaming should either resume with exactly the remaining tokens (no duplication) or the server should send a clean terminal event with full Unicode boundary preserved. No partial grapheme or duplicated tokens should be observable to the client.

Note: customer provided packet capture and Application logs; see attached log excerpts below for timestamps and example event payloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a client that connects to /v1/stream with SSE and long-lived idle (~30s) between tokens.
2) Route traffic through CloudFront (default keepalive/idle-probe behavior).
3) Issue a generation with a relatively long final sentence (ensures streaming tail).
4) Wait for CloudFront idle probe or artificially lower keepalive to trigger probe, observe reconnect sequence and final tokens delivered to client.
5) Repeat 50-200 times to reproduce at low probability; customer saw ~3% occurrence under their traffic pattern.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kumar (Support): Received initial report from ByteForge. They included browser console logs and a pcap showing intermittent duplication after CloudFront probe. Marking as P1 due to customer impact and frequency under their workload.

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Acknowledged. Asked for exact request IDs and times. Requested the customer's CloudFront config (idle timeout) and whether they use HTTP/2 multiplexing through CloudFront.

2026-03-11 - Customer (ByteForge): Provided sample request IDs: r-20260309-1872, r-20260309-1899 and confirmed CloudFront default idle timeout (60s) but they have additional nginx-h2 edge with keepalive 20s.

2026-03-11 - Mateo Chen (Runtime Eng): Initial hypothesis: proxy half-close during CloudFront probe may cause the client to re-issue small buffered chunk and server duplicate last in-flight token when the session is reattached. Also observed potential UTF-8 boundary split when chunking occurs at multi-byte codepoint.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Ran controlled reproducer in staging with CloudFront-like probe. Successfully produced duplicate short token in 1/40 runs and observed incomplete UTF-8 when chunk boundary fell inside a 4-byte emoji sequence.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: CloudFront idle probe causes upstream half-close; our streaming-proxy tries to reattach session and retransmit in-flight buffer leading to duplicate short sequence.
Hypothesis 2: The proxy/chunking path is splitting on raw bytes without ensuring UTF-8 grapheme boundaries; when retransmit collides with a split boundary, client displays replacement char (U+FFFD).

Evidence: pcap shows FIN/ACK from CloudFront then immediate new connection; server-side logs show re-queued chunk with same sequence id. Reproducer in staging shows duplication probability increases when keepalive shorter (20s).
Telemetry: token-level trace shows last two mini-chunks re-emitted with same sequence id in duplicated cases (trace r-20260309-1872).

Mitigations tested: a) Server-side dedupe on sequence-id prevented visible duplicate but left partial UTF-8 artifact in one run. b) Buffering to align on UTF-8 codepoint boundaries eliminated replacement char but introduced ~6-12ms tail latency in staging.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: Enabled UTF-8-safe chunk alignment in streaming-proxy for ByteForge account (feature-flagged) and added a short dedupe window (idempotency of last-in-flight chunk) to suppress immediate duplicate emission. Customer opted for UTF-8-safe alignment + dedupe. Post-change telemetry (24h) shows duplication reduced to <0.1% and no replacement-char events observed.

Planned permanent fix: 1) upstream: make chunking component UTF-8 grapheme-aware by default to avoid splitting multi-byte codepoints; 2) add idempotent resume handshake to prevent retransmit of already acknowledged chunk sequence; 3) update streaming runbook to include CDN keepalive guidance and a diagnostic flag to surface half-close events.

Follow-ups: Create INT task to roll UTF-8-safe chunking to all customers behind a gradual rollout (INT-3301). Add a dashboard alert for half-close retransmit rate exceeding 0.5% per customer.
workaround_steps: 1) Enable account-scoped feature flag: 'utf8-aligned-chunking' (internal flag name: ff/utf8_chunk_align).
2) Enable request-scoped dedupe window: temporarily ignore retransmit of a sequence id within 250ms of original emission.
3) Recommend customer to set CloudFront idle timeout >= 120s or align nginx keepalive > CloudFront probe interval while we roll fix.
